plain: The Stanford scientist Garry Nolan, whom Michels calls both an immunologist and a microbiologist and a friend, is said to link UFO experiences to two connected parts of the brain's basal ganglia, the caudate nucleus and the putamen: people with more densely packed neurons there are supposedly more likely to see UFOs, and also more "psychic", more intuitive and better at executive functioning. Michels brings this up on several episodes, retelling Nolan's work in his own words. He calls it "working theories" that are "not definitive" in one place and "studies" in another, and on one occasion adds that the trait runs in families, which would suggest that seeing UFOs is partly inherited.
